result:

    "title": "Shifted from pull-based to push-based indexing via daemon and filesystem queue to capture all git operations with minimal hook latency",
    "body": "Implemented a launchd-managed daemon that watches a filesystem queue (~/.diwa/queue/) for index operations enqueued by post-merge hooks. This addresses two critical gaps: (1) fast-forward pulls were being missed entirely because no post-merge hooks existed, leaving repositories with dozens of unindexed commits, and (2) synchronous hook execution risked user-facing latency. By moving to async background processing, hook latency dropped below 10ms (avoiding expensive ORT loads at enqueue time) while naturally debouncing bursty activity from operations like multi-commit git pulls. Seamless migration via `diwa migrate` in Homebrew's post_install hook ensures existing users get the new daemon-based system without manual intervention or data loss.",
